## `ChatLayout`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.ChatLayout` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Bubble geometry for the chat view: widths, padding, where each bubble sits. Text measurement is the engine's; everything after it is here, pure and unit-tested. Units are canvas units.

<a id="chatlayout--bubbleshare"></a>

### `const float BubbleShare = 0.8f`

Largest share of the row a character or player bubble takes.

<a id="chatlayout--buttongap"></a>

### `const float ButtonGap = 6.0f`

Space above the button row and between two bubble buttons.

<a id="chatlayout--buttonheight"></a>

### `const float ButtonHeight = 28.0f`

Height of a bubble button.

<a id="chatlayout--margin"></a>

### `const float Margin = 10.0f`

Space between the content's edges and the bubbles.

<a id="chatlayout--padx"></a>

### `const float PadX = 14.0f`

Text inset inside a bubble, left and right.

<a id="chatlayout--pady"></a>

### `const float PadY = 10.0f`

Text inset inside a bubble, top and bottom. Also the room Thai tone marks stacked above an upper vowel need above the first line (about 4 units over the line box).

<a id="chatlayout--spacing"></a>

### `const float Spacing = 10.0f`

Vertical space between two bubbles.

<a id="chatlayout--wrapslack"></a>

### `const float WrapSlack = 2.0f`

Extra width given to measured text so the engine never wraps it one word earlier.

<a id="chatlayout--bubblesize"></a>

### `static void BubbleSize(float textWidth, float textHeight, float buttonsWidth, bool hasButtons, float maxTextWidth, out float width, out float height)`

A bubble's size from its measured text and its buttons.

**Parameters**

- `textWidth`: Measured text width (at most [`ChatLayout.TextMaxWidth`](#chatlayout--textmaxwidth)).
- `textHeight`: Measured text height.
- `buttonsWidth`: Width of the button row (buttons and gaps), 0 for none.
- `hasButtons`: True when the bubble has buttons.
- `maxTextWidth`: The limit the text was measured at.
- `width`: The bubble's width.
- `height`: The bubble's height.

<a id="chatlayout--left"></a>

### `static float Left(CwyChatRole role, float viewportWidth, float bubbleWidth)`

The bubble's left edge: the character's on the left, the player's on the right, system notes centred.

**Parameters**

- `role`: Whose bubble.
- `viewportWidth`: The chat view's inner width.
- `bubbleWidth`: The bubble's width.

<a id="chatlayout--stack"></a>

### `static float Stack(IReadOnlyList<float> heights, float[] tops)`

Stacks bubbles top to bottom.

**Parameters**

- `heights`: Each bubble's height, oldest first.
- `tops`: Receives each bubble's top (same length as `heights`).

**Returns:** The content's height.

<a id="chatlayout--textmaxwidth"></a>

### `static float TextMaxWidth(float viewportWidth, CwyChatRole role)`

The widest a bubble's text may be.

**Parameters**

- `viewportWidth`: The chat view's inner width.
- `role`: Whose bubble.

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.CwyInputSpec` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

Base: [`CwyPartSpec`](#cwypartspec)

A text box in the game's style. Typing goes through the operating system's input method (Thai, Japanese composition), and no hotkey fires while it has the keyboard.

<a id="cwyinputspec--ctor"></a>

### `CwyInputSpec(string id)`

Creates an input part.

**Parameters**

- `id`: The part's id.

<a id="cwyinputspec--clearonsubmit"></a>

### `bool ClearOnSubmit { get; set; }`

True to empty the box after it sent its text.

<a id="cwyinputspec--lines"></a>

### `int Lines { get; set; }`

Visible lines (1-12). 1 is a one-line box; more lines wrap and scroll inside the box.

<a id="cwyinputspec--maxlength"></a>

### `int MaxLength { get; set; }`

Most characters the box accepts; 0 for no limit (up to 20000).

<a id="cwyinputspec--placeholder"></a>

### `string Placeholder { get; set; }`

Grey text shown while the box is empty.

<a id="cwyinputspec--submitonenter"></a>

### `bool SubmitOnEnter { get; set; }`

True (default): Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line. False: Enter starts a new line and Ctrl+Enter (Command+Enter on a Mac) sends. A one-line box always sends on Enter.

## `CwyRichText`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.CwyRichText` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Helpers for TextMeshPro rich text in text parts ([`ICwyTextView`](#icwytextview)).

<a id="cwyrichtext--escape"></a>

### `static string Escape(string text)`

Text shown exactly as written: wrapped in `<noparse>`, with any `</noparse>` inside broken by an invisible zero-width space so it cannot end the wrapper early. Use it for anything a player, a file or a language model wrote.

**Parameters**

- `text`: Untrusted text; null is empty.

<a id="cwywindowspec"></a>

## `CwyWindowSpec`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.CwyWindowSpec` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

What a mod window is built with: its id, title, size rules and parts, stacked top to bottom in the order of [`CwyWindowSpec.Parts`](#cwywindowspec--parts). Hand it to `helper.Ui.CreateWindow`.

**Example**

```csharp
var spec = new CwyWindowSpec("chat")
{
    Title = "Satone",
    Width = 640f,
    Height = 720f,
    CloseOnEscape = false,               // Esc only takes the keyboard away
    Parts =
    {
        new CwyChatSpec("log"),
        new CwyInputSpec("say") { Placeholder = "Type here", Lines = 3 },
        new CwyButtonsSpec("actions") { Buttons = { new CwyButtonSpec("send", "Send") } },
    },
};
```

<a id="cwywindowspec--ctor"></a>

### `CwyWindowSpec(string id)`

Creates a spec.

**Parameters**

- `id`: The window's id within the mod, e.g. `chat`: 1-48 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, not starting with a dot. It names the window's object (`CWY.Mod.<modId>.<id>`) and the key its remembered place is stored under.

<a id="cwywindowspec--defaultminheight"></a>

### `const float DefaultMinHeight = 280.0f`

Default smallest height, in canvas units.

<a id="cwywindowspec--defaultminwidth"></a>

### `const float DefaultMinWidth = 420.0f`

Default smallest width, in canvas units (1920x1080 reference).

<a id="cwywindowspec--closeonescape"></a>

### `bool CloseOnEscape { get; set; }`

What Escape does while the player is in this window. True: the window closes (as its close button does). False: Escape only takes the keyboard away from the window's text box, and an Escape with no text box selected is the game's again.

<a id="cwywindowspec--followhideui"></a>

### `bool FollowHideUi { get; set; }`

True to fade out with the game's Hide UI button and come back with it.

<a id="cwywindowspec--height"></a>

### `float Height { get; set; }`

Preferred height in canvas units on first open; 0 uses the default share of the screen.

<a id="cwywindowspec--hideonclose"></a>

### `bool HideOnClose { get; set; }`

True: the close button and Escape hide the window, then raise [`ICwyWindow.CloseRequested`](#icwywindow--closerequested). False: they only raise it and the mod decides.

<a id="cwywindowspec--id"></a>

### `string Id { get; }`

The window's id within the mod.

<a id="cwywindowspec--minheight"></a>

### `float MinHeight { get; set; }`

Smallest height the player can resize to. Raised automatically when the parts need more.

<a id="cwywindowspec--minwidth"></a>

### `float MinWidth { get; set; }`

Smallest width the player can resize to. Raised automatically when the parts need more.

<a id="cwywindowspec--parts"></a>

The parts, top to bottom.

<a id="cwywindowspec--rememberrect"></a>

True to reopen the window where the player last left it (also across game restarts).

<a id="cwywindowspec--resizable"></a>

## `EscapeAction`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.EscapeAction` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What Escape does this frame, as far as mod windows are concerned.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="escapeaction--game"></a>`Game` | 0 | The game's: it handles Escape as it always does (fullscreen to windowed). |
| <a id="escapeaction--console"></a>`Console` | 1 | The CWY console's: it closes (`ConsoleEscapeGuard`). Mod windows do nothing. |
| <a id="escapeaction--inputmethod"></a>`InputMethod` | 2 | The input method's: Escape cancels a composition in a mod window's text box. Nothing else happens. |
| <a id="escapeaction--closewindow"></a>`CloseWindow` | 3 | A mod window closes ([`CwyWindowSpec.CloseOnEscape`](#cwywindowspec--closeonescape)). |
| <a id="escapeaction--releasekeyboard"></a>`ReleaseKeyboard` | 4 | A mod window's text box gives the keyboard back; the window stays. |

<a id="escaperouting"></a>

## `EscapeRouting`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.EscapeRouting` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Focus isolation for mod windows, generalising the console's Escape rule: who an Escape belongs to when mod windows, the console and the game's own fields may all be on screen. Pure, so every rule is unit-tested.

In priority order:

1. The console already closed on this Escape: nobody else acts.
2. A mod window's text box has the keyboard: composing → the input method cancels the composition, nothing else; otherwise the window closes, or with [`CwyWindowSpec.CloseOnEscape`](#cwywindowspec--closeonescape) off its text box lets go of the keyboard. The console stands down by its own rule (another text field is selected), and the game's switch to windowed mode is skipped.
3. One of the game's text fields has the keyboard: the game's.
4. The console is open and would take it: the console's.
5. The player is in a mod window that closes on Escape: it closes.
6. Otherwise the game's.

Hotkeys need no rule here: the framework's registry ignores every chord while any text field is selected (`Hotkeys.IsTyping`), and in the room the game reads no key but Escape (`RoomGameManager`; `CameraManager`/`Camera_Controller` are not in `RoomScene`).

<a id="escaperouting--decide"></a>

### `static EscapeDecision Decide(EscapeInputs inputs)`

Decides who an Escape belongs to.

**Parameters**

- `inputs`: Who has the keyboard.

<a id="scrollstate"></a>

## `ScrollState`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.ScrollState` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Where a scrolling view is, in content units, and whether it follows the end: the chat view (follows the newest bubble unless the player scrolled up) and the list view (starts at the top). Pure, so it is unit-tested.

[`ScrollState.Top`](#scrollstate--top) is the content's distance above the viewport's top edge. Following means "stay at the bottom while content grows": a streamed reply keeps scrolling into view, but once the player scrolls up the view stays on what they are reading, and scrolling back to the bottom follows again. Content dropped above the view (the oldest bubbles past the cap) is subtracted from [`ScrollState.Top`](#scrollstate--top), so the lines being read do not jump.

<a id="scrollstate--ctor"></a>

### `ScrollState(bool followEnd)`

Creates a state.

**Parameters**

- `followEnd`: True to start following the end (chat); false to start at the top (list).

How close to the bottom (in content units) still counts as "at the bottom".

Smallest scrollbar handle, as a share of the track.

<a id="scrollstate--content"></a>

True while the view stays at the bottom as content grows.

<a id="scrollstate--top"></a>

<a id="textboxkeys"></a>

## `TextBoxKeys`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.TextBoxKeys` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The keys of a mod window's text box: Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line, and nothing a chord or the input method used is inserted. Pure, so every rule is unit-tested.

What the game's TextMeshPro hands over (`TMP_InputField.KeyPressed`, multi-line-newline mode): Return and keypad Enter arrive as `'\n'` (`'\r'` and macOS's Ctrl+C, U+0003, are turned into it), and with Shift held as a vertical tab `'\v'`.

While the operating system's input method is composing (Japanese Kotoeri; Thai layouts never compose), and on the frame its composition ended, Enter commits the composition: it must neither send nor break the line.

The console's one-line field keeps its own rule (`ConsoleKeyRouter.ClassifyTypedChar`); this one adds the second line and the composition guard for mod windows.

<a id="textboxkeys--classify"></a>

### `static TextBoxChar Classify(char c, bool control, bool command, bool alt, bool multiLine, bool submitOnEnter, bool composing, bool pasting = false)`

Classifies one character.

**Parameters**

- `c`: The character the text box is about to insert.
- `control`: A Control key is held.
- `command`: A Command (macOS) key is held.
- `alt`: An Alt / Option key is held (AltGr is Ctrl+Alt on Windows and types characters).
- `multiLine`: The box shows more than one line.
- `submitOnEnter`: Enter sends (true) or breaks the line (false; then Ctrl/Command+Enter sends).
- `composing`: The input method is composing now or finished composing this frame or the last.
- `pasting`: The character is part of a paste (Command/Ctrl+V is down): TextMeshPro appends the clipboard one character at a time with the chord still held (`TMP_InputField`), so the chord rule would drop all of it. Printable characters are kept, a line break becomes a new line in a multi-line box and is dropped in a one-line box - a paste never sends.

<a id="textboxkeys--composingrecently"></a>

### `static bool ComposingRecently(bool composingNow, int frame, int lastComposingFrame)`

True when an Enter now belongs to the input method: it is composing, or it was composing on this frame or the one before (the frame the commit cleared the composition).

**Parameters**

<a id="windowescapeguard"></a>

## `WindowEscapeGuard`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.WindowEscapeGuard` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Keeps the game from acting on an Escape a mod window used: the game reads Escape itself in `RoomGameManager.Update` and calls `SettingService.ChangeWindowMode(Window)`, which would drop a fullscreen game to windowed (the same problem the console's `ConsoleEscapeGuard` solves).

Mod windows decide and act on Escape in `LateUpdate`, after every `Update` - so after the console and the game have read the key - and record there who would own an Escape pressed on the next frame ([`WindowEscapeGuard.Observe`](#windowescapeguard--observe)). The game's switch is skipped when that word is fresh (this frame or the last), says a mod window, and Escape went down this frame. Main thread only.

<a id="windowescapeguard--noframe"></a>

### `const int NoFrame = -2147483648`

Frame number meaning "never".

<a id="windowescapeguard--blockedcount"></a>

### `long BlockedCount { get; }`

How many switches to windowed mode were skipped.

<a id="windowescapeguard--observedframe"></a>

### `int ObservedFrame { get; }`

The frame of the latest [`WindowEscapeGuard.Observe`](#windowescapeguard--observe).

<a id="windowescapeguard--observedowns"></a>

### `bool ObservedOwns { get; }`

Whether the latest observation said a mod window owns Escape.

<a id="windowescapeguard--observe"></a>

### `void Observe(int frame, bool modWindowOwns)`

Records who would own an Escape now. Call once a frame.

**Parameters**

- `frame`: Unity's frame number.
- `modWindowOwns`: True when a mod window would take it ([`EscapeDecision.ModWindowOwns`](#escapedecision--modwindowowns)).

<a id="windowescapeguard--reset"></a>

### `void Reset()`

Forgets the observation. For tests.

<a id="windowescapeguard--shouldblockwindowedswitch"></a>

### `bool ShouldBlockWindowedSwitch(int frame, bool toWindowed, bool escapeDown)`

True when the game's switch to windowed mode must be skipped. Counts each skip.

**Parameters**

- `frame`: Unity's frame number.
- `toWindowed`: The game asked for windowed mode.
- `escapeDown`: Escape went down this frame.

<a id="windowrectstore"></a>

## `WindowRectStore`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.WindowRectStore` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Where the player last left each mod window, by `<modId>/<windowId>`. Pure: the adapter reads and writes the file (`BepInEx/data/ui/windows.json`).

The file:

```csharp
{ "schema": 1, "windows": { "my.mod/chat": { "left": 1210, "top": 80, "width": 640, "height": 720 } } }
```

Values are canvas units at the game's 1920x1080 reference scaling. A remembered place is clamped onto the canvas when it is used ([`WindowRectMath.Clamp`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.md#windowrectmath--clamp)), so a smaller window or another aspect ratio never puts a window off screen. An entry that does not parse is skipped and named in the problem text; the rest still load.

<a id="windowrectstore--maxcoordinate"></a>

### `const float MaxCoordinate = 100000.0f`

Largest coordinate or size accepted (canvas units).

<a id="windowrectstore--maxentries"></a>

Most windows remembered; the file is cleared of the rest on the next save.

### `int Count { get; }`

<a id="windowstack"></a>

## `WindowStack`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Ui.WindowStack` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The mod windows' order and which one the player is "in". Pure; the game adapter mirrors the order onto the overlay canvas (last sibling = on top).

A window becomes [`WindowStack.Active`](#windowstack--active) when it is shown or the player presses a mouse button over it, and stops being active when the player presses a button anywhere outside every CWY window (the room, the game's own UI), or when it is hidden or removed. The active window is the one an Escape with no text box selected belongs to ([`EscapeRouting`](#escaperouting)), so clicking the room hands Escape back to the game.

Not thread-safe: main thread only, like the windows it orders.

<a id="windowstack--active"></a>

The window the player is in, or null.
